headline: Speed hump program would switch from council petitions to yearly applications, under plan presented by transportation commissioner
summary: The city has more than 70 permanent speed humps and installs about 35 temporary ones each year, according to the transportation commissioner's report. Residents would apply with co-signers from their street, and fire department approval would be needed for speed humps on primary emergency routes. Staff would bring one yearly program to the council, and pending petitions would become applications. Elsewhere, the Holden Street truck ban petition was filed, and the Lake Avenue all-way stop request was held until January.
decisions: Approved removing the handicap parking space at 52 Ward Street.
Approved one handicap parking space at 243 Tacoma Street, not two.
Approved removing the handicap parking space in front of 1 Kingsbury Street.
Held the handicap parking space request for 20 Worth Street.
Approved a handicap parking space at 15 Airlie Street, designated for loading only, so a vehicle can pick up or drop off.
Approved removing the handicap parking space in front of 63 Arline Street.
Held the Caroline Street handicap space request so staff can consider removing both spaces, not moving one.
Filed the Holden Street truck ban petition.
Held the request to replace the winter parking ban on Henrieta Street with a no-parking ban on the odd side when declared.
Approved flashing crosswalk signs at both crosswalks near Winthrop Street and Vernon Street, pending funding.
Approved a no-parking-anytime zone across the driveway of 48 Windham Street.
Approved a no-parking here to corner sign on Wall Street at Thorn Street.
Approved increased speed and traffic enforcement on Mayrose Street.
Held the Clover Street stop sign requests (7A, 7B, 7C) for re-advertising, and asked that the stop signs that were never ordained be removed by Chair's order.
Held the all-way stop request at Lake Avenue and Bigelow Davis Parkway until the January meeting.
Approved a review of the traffic signal timing at Southbridge Street and Hammond Street.
Filed the request for turtle crossing signs on Massasoit Road.
Filed the request for a yield to blind driveway sign at 25 Salisbury Street.
Filed the request for waterfowl crossing signs on Stafford Street.
Filed the request for wayfinding signs directing trucks to Mass 12 from West Boylston Street.
Approved Do Not Block Intersection signs on Pleasant Street, facing westbound traffic, plus a Chair's order for speed limit signs on Pleasant Street.
Approved additional one-way signage and moving one set of signs on Fairmount Avenue at Dartmouth Street.
Approved an additional set of one-way signs on Fairmount Avenue at Clarendon Street.
Filed the request for a declared winter parking ban with no parking on both sides of Dora Street.
Filed the request to move the winter parking ban on Danielle Street to the odd side.
Filed the informational report on e-scooter and e-bike regulations.
Approved the new speed hump program, which replaces council petitions with yearly applications.
discussion: Speed hump program: The transportation commissioner's report proposes applications in place of council petitions. Applications would need co-signers from the street, or a district councilor could file one. Speed tables or low-profile humps would be used on secondary streets.

Holden Street truck ban: Public speakers asked for a ban at Shore Drive and Norton Drive and raised concerns about speeding, school buses, and heavy trucks. Transportation staff said MassDOT decides on truck routes, and a Holden Street truck study is already approved and waits for funding.

Lake Avenue all-way stop: Transportation staff said there were 32 crashes at this intersection over five years and about 15,000 vehicles a day on Lake Avenue. Staff said all-way stops are hard to do safely on a divided road, and asked to hold the item until the January meeting.

Henrieta Street winter parking: A public speaker said a car was towed for $250 during a storm. Staff said DPW had concerns about switching the ban to the odd side because of the street's cross slope, so the item was held.

Dora and Danielle winter bans: Dora Street residents spoke against a ban on both sides, citing a resident's need to drive to work. A Danielle Street resident asked to keep parking on the odd side and said residents clear the snow themselves.
